title: Gluten-Free Almond Maple Granola Clusters
changes_from_base: Gluten-free: certified gluten-free oats are bound with ground almonds, rice flour and a melted maple and dark brown sugar syrup, pressed into the tray, baked and scored so it snaps into clusters; no nuts, seeds or raisins.
summary: These gluten-free clusters are studded with ground almonds and bound with maple syrup, resulting in shards that are deeply golden, wonderfully nutty and satisfyingly crunchy.
equipment: large rimmed baking tray (about 33 x 46 cm)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan) with the shelf in the middle and line a large rimmed baking tray with baking paper.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine 510 g gluten-free rolled oats, 140 g almond flour, 70 g gluten-free brown rice flour and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: In a medium saucepan over low heat, gently warm 120 ml rapeseed oil, 200 g dark brown sugar and 120 ml maple syrup, stirring often, until the sugar dissolves; turn off the heat and stir in 1 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the warm syrup over the oat mixture and stir thoroughly until every grain is coated.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Tip onto the lined tray and press very firmly with a rigid metal spatula into one even, compact layer.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Place in the oven for 45 min, rotating halfway through, until golden and wonderfully fragrant.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Let cool right through on the tray, which helps it crisp up.

steps.title: Score
steps.text: Whilst still slightly warm, use a sharp knife to score the slab into bars or squares; once cooled through, snap along the score lines.

tips: Stir the ground almonds evenly through the oats so the maple syrup binds everything into firm clusters.
Press the mixture very firmly before baking to keep clusters from crumbling
Cool completely on the tray before breaking apart so they set properly
safety: Use oats labelled gluten-free if you are cooking for anyone who avoids gluten, as ordinary oats are often cross-contaminated with wheat
storage: Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
